title: Coherent projective quotients, Euler characteristics and regularity under field extension
statement:
Let $L/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension], let $n\geq0$ and $r\geq1$, and put $X=\mathbf P^n_k$ and $X_L=\mathbf P^n_L$. Let $p:X_L\to X$ be the projection induced by extension of coefficients. Use coherent modules [pqf-def-coherent], pullbacks $E_L=p^*E$ [def-pc-module-pullback], twists $E(d)=E\otimes\mathcal O_X(d)$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist], module sheaf cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology], finite vector-space dimensions [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] and Euler characteristics [def-pc-euler-characteristic]. Then $p^*\mathcal O_X^{\oplus r}\cong\mathcal O_{X_L}^{\oplus r}$. Pullback of any short exact sequence $0\to K\to\mathcal O_X^{\oplus r}\to F\to0$ of coherent modules is a short exact sequence of coherent modules $0\to K_L\to\mathcal O_{X_L}^{\oplus r}\to F_L\to0$. For every coherent module $E$ on $X$, $E_L$ is coherent and $p^*(E(d))\cong E_L(d)$ for every integer $d$. For every $q\geq0$ and integer $d$ the natural base-change map is an isomorphism
$$H^q(X,E(d))\otimes_k L\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(X_L,E_L(d)),$$
and the two finite dimensions over their respective fields are equal. Consequently
$$\chi(X_L,E_L(d))=\chi(X,E(d))$$
for every integer $d$, and, for every integer $a$,
$$\bigl[H^j(X,E(a-j))=0\ (1\leq j\leq n)\bigr]\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \bigl[H^j(X_L,E_L(a-j))=0\ (1\leq j\leq n)\bigr].$$

proof.text:
Use homogeneous coordinate index set $\{0,\ldots,n\}$, which is finite and nonempty even for $n=0$. The Cartesian square of [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-pullback] identifies $X_L$ with $X	imes_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}L$, with $p$ the stated coefficient projection. The charts in [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] have rings $k[t_j:j
e i]$ and $L[t_j:j
e i]$; their transition maps send a coordinate ratio to the same ratio. These are also the standard opens of the polynomial Proj convention of the item: the degree-zero localization has the mutually inverse substitutions $t_j\mapsto x_j/x_i$ and $x^\alpha/x_i^{|\alpha|}\mapsto\prod_{j
e i}t_j^{\alpha_j}$. Thus the two projective-space conventions agree over the fields. Both spaces are proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], and locally Noetherian by [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft], since their affine charts are finite type over fields (a field is Noetherian because its only ideals are $0$ and the whole field). The finite standard cover makes $X	o\operatorname{Spec}k$ quasi-compact. Its pairwise chart intersections are the principal opens obtained by inverting $x_j/x_i$, hence affine and quasi-compact; consequently it is quasi-separated.

By [lem-pc-field-extension-flat], $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat, with no algebraicity or finiteness assumption on $L/k$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] with its flat morphism $f$ equal to $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and its base morphism $g$ equal to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. The resulting projection $X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}L\to X$ is $p$ by step 1, so $p$ is flat. Apply the exactness assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-pullback-exact-pushforward-injective] to $p$: the pullback of the given short exact sequence is short exact as a sequence of Zariski module sheaves. This proves exactness, including injectivity on the left; coherence and the identification of the middle term are checked next.

source.place: Tags 01U9 (lemma-base-change-flat) and 02N4 (lemma-pullback-flat); varieties.tex, Tag 08AG (lemma-bound-quotients-free), first field-extension reduction

proof.text: For any coherent $E$ on $X$, [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] says that $E$ is quasi-coherent and of finite type. Its pullback is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent] and of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-finite-type]. Since $X_L$ is locally Noetherian by step 1, the reverse implication of [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] proves that $E_L$ is coherent. Apply this separately to $K$, $F$, and the middle coherent module of the given sequence.

The adjunction in [def-pc-module-pullback] makes $p^*$ preserve finite direct sums, and [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf] identifies $p^*\mathcal O_X$ with $\mathcal O_{X_L}$; apply it to each of the $r$ summands. For any $d\in\mathbf Z$, use the local frames $e_i^{(d)}$ of [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. On the $i$th chart, the identification $E(d)\cong E$, $s\otimes e_i^{(d)}\mapsto s$, pulls back to the identification with $E_L$. On an overlap its change of frame is multiplication by $(x_i/x_j)^d$, whose pullback is the same coordinate ratio over $L$. The local identities therefore glue to $p^*(E(d))\cong E_L(d)$. Coordinate ratios are units on overlaps, so this also applies to negative $d$. The same local identifications show that $E(d)$ and $E_L(d)$ are coherent, since coherence in [pqf-def-coherent] is local and invariant under isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01O3 (lemma-relative-proj-base-change), twist comparison; Tag 0095 (definition-pushforward), tensor pullback; explicit frame argument for arbitrary integers

proof.text: Fix $q\geq0$ and $d\in\mathbf Z$. Apply [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] to $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $g:\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the quasi-coherent module $E(d)$. Step 1 supplies the Cartesian square and the quasi-compact quasi-separated hypothesis; step 2 supplies flatness of $g$; steps 3--4 supply quasi-coherence and identify $(p^*E(d))$ with $E_L(d)$. The affine-base clause gives exactly the natural base-change isomorphism $H^q(X,E(d))\otimes_kL\to H^q(X_L,E_L(d))$, not just an unspecified vector-space isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 02KH (lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology), both clauses; varieties.tex, Tags 08A4 and 08AB, proofs

proof.text: The coherent-cohomology finiteness of [lem-pc-projective-space-coherent-finiteness], with the Noetherian ring $A=k$ or $A=L$, proves that both cohomology spaces in step 5 are finite-dimensional over their respective fields. Apply [lem-pc-finrank-field-base-change] to the finite-dimensional $k$-space $H^q(X,E(d))$. The symmetry $v\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\otimes v$ identifies the order of tensor factors there with the order in step 5, and the latter isomorphism identifies the resulting dimension with $\dim_L H^q(X_L,E_L(d))$. Thus the two finite dimensions asserted in the item are equal for every $q,d$.

By [lem-pc-projective-space-cohomology-bound], the quasi-coherent modules $E(d)$ and $E_L(d)$ have zero cohomology in all degrees greater than $n$. The Euler characteristics in [def-pc-euler-characteristic] are therefore the finite sums over $0\leq q\leq n$. Step 6 equates each summand, with the same sign $(-1)^q$, proving their equality for every integer $d$. A finite-dimensional vector space is zero exactly when its dimension is zero: a basis has no elements exactly in that case. Apply this observation to the equal dimensions of step 6 with $(q,d)=(j,a-j)$ for each $1\leq j\leq n$, and take their conjunction. This proves the stated equivalence for every $a\in\mathbf Z$. For $n=0$ the conjunction is empty on both sides and hence true.
